blocks.en: To evaluate ReLEAF's effectiveness and scalability, we developed mathematical models using historical agricultural records, weather data, and experimental measurements. Incorporating weather variables into 25 years of rice yield data reduced prediction error by 32% compared to the baseline trend model. We also modeled protectant activity, treatment timing, dosage, and production capacity to estimate the resources needed under different stress conditions. Finally, we evaluated the potential costs of deploying ReLEAF across Taiwan's 346 farming townships, connecting laboratory findings with real-world agricultural applications.

blocks.en: The case for precision came from natural farmers. Ms. Chen and Dr. Li (seen in IHP page), who farm in northwest Taiwan, maintain that raising a crop is like raising a child: a plant protected from every stress never builds the tolerance it would otherwise have. That sets the specification this index is built to. The reactor should produce only when a threshold that accurately reflects crop condition is crossed, so the 32% error reduction in the second crop is evidence for a release rule that initiates for the right reason. The index decides only whether to act; its demand level sets the light intensity in M2, and the amount that reaches the crop is settled in M4.

blocks.en: The activity term cancels out of the capital result. The dose is a volume of our own culture and the reactor's output is that same culture per day, so the secreted activity appears once in the numerator and once in the denominator of the vessel calculation. At 0.5 mU/mL or at 7.25, the two ends of our own DNPH readings, the answer is the same 81 L per hectare, and everything below the vessel line follows: the fleet, the capital and the payback do not depend on which reading is finally adopted. The activity figure sets the protectant tally in kU and the mass in grams, and whether the dose works at all, which no run of ours bounds.

blocks.en: What the capital does depend on is the harvest cycle. The throughput row is a concentration over a batch cycle of five hours, or 4.8 harvests a day, and a 72-hour reactor run read by anti-His ELISA does not support that: the concentration peaks at 12 h, holds its band of 2.5 to 6.5 µg/mL to 30 h, then falls to about half from 36 h on. DNPH on the same supernatants peaks six hours later, at 18 h. A 12-hour cycle puts the vessel at 195 L per hectare and the capital at US$9120; an 18-hour cycle puts them at 292 L and US$13 679. blocks.en: Eight things this model cannot yet do. Efficacy is unbounded: no plant run of ours constrains how much of a salinity loss the protectant takes back, so every figure in dollars is drawn against efficacy and never at a value. The dose is one that worked, not the smallest that works, and no dilution series has been run. The canopy correction is modeled and spans 1.68 to 3.52, and every row of the ledger below it inherits that. The concentration rests on a single supernatant assay below the quantitation limit, and the 28-hour endpoint that would check it cannot be distinguished from a stalled reaction. The harvest cycle of five hours behind the throughput row is the one bench number the capital result depends on, since the activity term cancels; a 72-hour ELISA run puts the concentration peak at 12 h and a halving after 30 h, which a five-hour cycle does not obviously fit, and at 12 or 18 hours the capital is US$9120 or US$13 679 a hectare instead of US$3800. Shelf life has no direct measurement. The figure standing in for it, an apparent half-time of 0.7 to 1.5 hours by two routes, comes from one unreplicated tube read in live culture while the cells were still producing; a replicated run rose over its first eight hours of light. Both bound activity in the vessel; neither reaches the lifetime of a harvested preparation, which is what the banked-stock plan turns on, and whether a concentrated, cooled or formulated stock lasts longer is untested. The protection window is assumed at two days per pass, which is what fixes a firing season at nine passes. The release rule is counted from waterlogging while the payback is priced on salinity; making them agree means rebuilding the rule around salt-sensitive growth stages. That would need roughly fifteen applications in a 30-day window instead of nine, or 81 reactor-days inside 30, which the current fleet could not serve for one hectare without banking far in advance.
